title: Multiply as whole numbers first
text: Ignore the decimal points and multiply $$6 \times 4$$. You will put the decimal point back by counting decimal places in the factors. A common mistake is to multiply $$0.6 \times 0.4$$ and keep only one decimal place. What is $$6 \times 4$$?

title: How many decimal places go in the product?
text: $$0.6$$ has 1 decimal place and $$0.4$$ has 1. The product has the sum of those counts. How many decimal places should the product show?

title: Worked solution
text: $$0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.24$$. The whole-number product 24 needs two decimal places, so it becomes 0.24. Common mistake: answering $$2.4$$ by keeping only one decimal place, or adding the decimals to get $$1.0$$. General rule: multiply the digits as whole numbers, then give the product as many decimal places as the factors have together.
